**Defining the Website's Purpose**

I'm starting with a deep dive into the goal: a premium website for Mikaela - Manager (MKS). I'm focusing on user expectations, aiming for a boutique feel. The information provided outlines the site's introduction and core services, like reservations, hosting, cleaning, and interior design. My focus is now on the initial user experience and how to best showcase Mikaela's services.


**Refining the Website Design**

I'm now zeroing in on the aesthetic, drawing from our target audience and desired vibe. The color palette will center on neutral tones, with serif fonts for headings and sans-serif for body text. I've also outlined the proposed site structure, planning dedicated pages for Services, Pricing, and Photography, ensuring a clean and intuitive user journey. The tech stack will utilize React and TypeScript.


**Mapping the Technical Components**

I'm now nailing down the tech specs. I'll use standard React hooks for navigation, avoiding external libraries for now, like React Router, and I'll keep the transitions lightweight using standard CSS or Tailwind. I'm focusing on simplicity, so the visual aspects are integrated but uncomplicated, to keep the core of the project solid. The goal is maintainability, while delivering the core functionality of the website. I have moved away from libraries such as React Router, and Framer Motion.
I am now developing the content for the website.


**Outlining Pricing and Components**

I've outlined all the pricing, by unit and guest count, as well as the photography packages and add-ons. I'm now developing the component designs, starting with the `App.tsx` layout and routing. I'll include a sticky navbar that transitions on scroll. The visual aspects have generous spacing.


**Detailing the Visual Design**

I'm now diving into the specific design elements. My color scheme is finalized: `bg-stone-50`, `text-stone-800`, and `border-stone-200`, with gold/bronze accents (`text-amber-700`) for a touch of subtle luxury. This will create a clean, elegant aesthetic. I'll make sure to integrate the branding to build a cohesive visual system.

\n\n

**Planning Component Architecture**

I've formulated a solid implementation plan: I'll start with setup, then move to the main app structure, and then build the individual components. My code plan focuses on the design and implementation of the site's various pages: `Home`, `About`, `Services`, `Pricing`, and `Photography`. I'll use a `HashRouter` for navigation.


**Confirming Navigation State**

I'm now implementing the navigation, and I'm focused on the active state. I'll make sure it's visually clear using the `Playfair Display` font and cream colors for a boutique feel. I am re-examining the original instructions, as the prompt is simply to build a website with specific information, so I will stick to static content only. Finally, I will review the pricing logic for accuracy.


**Structuring the Service Pages**

I'm now separating the cleaning and photography pricing into distinct sections under a "Pricing" page. I'll maintain a boutique feel by ensuring clear and concise information. I'll need to figure out how to best display tables on mobile screens, perhaps using a card view or scrollable containers. I'm focusing on responsiveness and clarity for the cleaning pricing structure, and how best to group this into a single page.
